decisions.reason: After a full year on the market, this handle family remains tightly connected to the firm's core engineering, finishing and specification capabilities, so accumulated market feedback is more likely to support incremental refinement than withdrawal.

The mitred handle family is somewhat more design-niche and therefore carries the highest pruning risk among the retained lines, but it still builds on familiar metalworking and architectural design knowledge that favors keeping it in the portfolio.

Its multifunctional character fits the firm's barrier-free, compliance and system-solution direction, and that strong knowledge relatedness gives management good scope to learn from use cases and improve it commercially.
As a standard door lever handle line, it sits in the firm's deepest absorptive-capacity domain and supports the continuity valued by architects and specifiers, making discontinuation unlikely.

This collection has the strongest external validation through its dedicated positioning and design-award recognition, so management would be very unlikely to remove it while it reinforces the brand's architecture-led product family strategy.
